title: When Rank Leaves the Room: Lessons from Intelligence to Acting
gist: A Marine Pulse podcast episode features retired Marine lieutenant colonel Matt Worsham, who moved from signals intelligence to a technology career and now to acting. He reflects on the tight-knit Marine SIGINT community and on veterans' civilian transitions, emphasizing that no one owes veterans anything.

insights.claim: Retired Marine lieutenant colonel Matt Worsham, a prior enlisted intelligence officer, transitioned first into a technology career and then into acting, co-hosting a production called The REEL DMV.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Illustrates non-linear veteran career paths relevant to workforce and transition-support themes.
insights.locator: Gary sits down with retired Marine lieutenant colonel

insights.claim: Worsham argues that no one owes veterans anything, framing civilian success as something transitioning service members must earn rather than expect.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: A self-reliance framing on veteran transition that pushes against entitlement-based support narratives.
insights.locator: with Matt emphasizing that no one owes veterans anything

insights.claim: Losing a job at Microsoft is what led Worsham into an acting career, and he discusses how commanders can help Marines develop identities beyond their military roles.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Speaks to identity and resilience issues in military-to-civilian transitions that shape retention and readiness debates.
